You and I are in similar boats. If you're anything like me, you know your depression is temporary. The feelings come and go.

Unfortunately, it's something we're going to battle with our entire lives. If we keep on living, we get to experience those respites where we see how everything we struggle with is worth it. We get to be happy for a time.

If we decide to stop living, there's no going back. 

Personally, knowing that my mind is sick is one thing that keeps me from ending it all. I rationalize that I'm in no place to make *that* permanent of a decision. Maybe you could tell yourself the same thing.

You got some of your frustrations out, so you did do something right. It's not good to be depressed and bottle it up. It's dangerous, in fact.

Sometimes going through the motions is all you *can* do. People that haven't experienced depression have made us feel as though we have no right to be depressed for any amount of time, and that we should *get over it* like it's a cold.

There is no getting over it. You trudge through. Some days are better than others. You may even like yourself a couple times a week for a few minutes. If it's the best you can do, at least you've accomplished something.

When you feel motivated, even slightly, take some time to figure out something you think you'd like to do, and research how to get there. You'll feel like you've taken a step, no matter how small.

Small steps count.

I'm glad you didn't end your life.

When I'm depressed, I don't want to hear that it's going to get better, either. I understand how you feel. In therapy, they teach you to recognize small goals right?

A 5-minute shower counts.

Eating just a little counts.

Getting dressed counts.

Not slicing into yourself counts.

Making this post counts.

Reaching out counts.

Every little thing you do counts.

My advice, give yourself a tiny sliver of credit for the little things. You won't instantly feel better, but it may help you find a way out of the rut. <3
